_: Published geometry for what San Francisco decided outside its own boundary. Emitted by pipeline/scripts/us_sf_reach/build_reach_geom.py. Coordinates live in reach/geom.qc; this file is the index and the provenance.

projection.note: cosl is frozen at San Francisco's latitude, so east-west scale drifts with distance from 37.76. The drift is measured per feature into proj_worst_m and each feature also carries its true lon/lat bounding box.

simplify.method: Douglas-Peucker, topology preserving, in world metres
simplify.note: measured as the largest distance from any ORIGINAL vertex to the simplified ring. Nothing is dropped for being small; a shape ships whole or not at all.

outside_test.test: the polygon's representative point is outside the ring, and further out than min_m
dropped_names: VACANT LAND - CARROLL AVE WATER LOT
WEST OF AQUATIC PARK MARINE LOTS
outside_test.note: the dropped rows are all waterfront: two DataSF registers disagreeing about where the shoreline is by tens of metres. The band between the furthest dropped and the nearest kept is empty, which is why the cut can be stated rather than argued.

not_drawn.thing: the Mountain Tunnel — Hetch Hetchy Reservoir to Moccasin
not_drawn.why: NHD's named 'Hetch Hetchy Aqueduct' feature stops at Moccasin. The upper reach is not in it, and nothing here will connect the reservoir to the line's east end with a segment we drew.

not_drawn.thing: the Farallones' own reach beyond the published boundary ring
not_drawn.why: the islands ship because txuc-3kzm contains them. Nothing else about them is asserted.

none is published. The FAA's aviation services carry runways and aprons and never property; Caltrans, TIGER and OSM all publish a facility footprint and they disagree by 15 %. The polygon here is labelled a footprint.

not_drawn.thing: the aqueduct's tunnels as separate objects
not_drawn.why: OpenStreetMap identifies them individually and its members carry source=NHD, i.e. they were seeded from the same federal line and hand-refined. Until that hand-refinement is checked, the federal line is the one that ships.

caltrans-airports.title: Airport Boundaries (CHaviation)
caltrans-airports.what: OBJECTID 218, the SFO polygon that matches the real footprint
caltrans-airports.trap: Caltrans ships TWO SFO polygons. OBJECTID 208 is larger and runs far east into the Bay and is not the airport. This file carries 218 and not 208.

cpad-2026a.publisher: GreenInfo Network — California Protected Areas Database
cpad-2026a.title: CPAD Holdings, current release
cpad-2026a.what: 255 parcel-aligned holdings whose owner is 'San Francisco - Public Utilities Commission, City and County of'
cpad-2026a.note: preferred over PAD-US 4.1, which is a dissolved 2023 re-publication of this same data — 15 blobs against 255 holdings. The endpoints advertised on data.ca.gov time out; this GreenInfo service is the reachable one.
cpad-2026a.trap: the Alameda watershed is filed under UNIT_NAME 'San Francisco Watershed Lands'. Querying 'SFPUC Alameda Watershed' returns 4 features, not 85.
cpad-2026a.derived: CPAD is itself compiled from county assessor and agency records; its lineage was not independently verified here.

gtnh-hgvs.title: City Lands
gtnh-hgvs.what: the city's own register of the land it owns
gtnh-hgvs.note: the dataset's own description says: "Not all lands are within the City and County proper. The City owns properties outside of its boundaries."

nhd-flowline.title: NHD Flowline (Large Scale), GNIS_NAME 'Hetch Hetchy Aqueduct'
nhd-flowline.what: 43 line features, one GNIS id (00243393), public domain

nhd-waterbody.title: NHD Waterbody (Large Scale)
nhd-waterbody.what: the reservoirs, by GNIS name, with the published surface area

nid.publisher: US Army Corps of Engineers — National Inventory of Dams
nid.title: NID CA00123
nid.what: O'Shaughnessy Dam: the coordinate, the height, the year and the owner
nid.note: GNIS carries NO dams in California — the class was retired — so a federal or state dam register is the only place this position exists. The NID row's own sourceAgency is 'California', i.e. the state DSOD.

tiger-arealm.title: Area Landmarks, California (tl_2024_06_arealm)
tiger-arealm.what: MTFCC K2582 (Cemetery) inside the Colma box
tiger-arealm.note: a file download; TIGERweb's REST service does not carry AREALM — verified negative. TIGER has Olivet Memorial Park and OpenStreetMap does not, so the obvious cartographic source is the incomplete one here.

txuc-3kzm.title: City and County of San Francisco boundary
txuc-3kzm.what: the LEGAL boundary, which is why the Farallon Islands are in it
txuc-3kzm.note: the same dataset base/coast is cut from; it runs kilometres into the Pacific and straight across the Golden Gate

features.name: City and County of San Francisco
features.note: the legal boundary, not the shoreline

features.name: Farallon Islands
features.note: California Government Code 23138: "The islands known as the Farralones (Farallons) are a part of said city and county." They are 50 km offshore and inside the same published boundary the map's own coastline is cut from.

features.name: Furman Bequest
features.note: 8 parcels of one bequest, in 4 Kern and Fresno county oil towns

features.name: San Antonio Pump Station / Sunol WTP Lands
SFPUC Peninsula Watershed
features.derived: the union of 103 published CPAD holdings. The parcels are CPAD's; the union is ours, and the acreage quoted is the sum of the holdings' own ACRES field, not a measurement of the unioned shape.

features.name: SFPUC Alameda Watershed
features.derived: the union of 85 published CPAD holdings. The parcels are CPAD's; the union is ours, and the acreage quoted is the sum of the holdings' own ACRES field, not a measurement of the unioned shape.
caveats: CPAD files the Alameda watershed under UNIT_NAME 'San Francisco Watershed Lands'. The name on this row is the one the SFPUC uses; the source's own string is carried in `unit_name`.

features.name: Sunol Regional Wilderness
features.derived: the union of 20 published CPAD holdings. The parcels are CPAD's; the union is ours, and the acreage quoted is the sum of the holdings' own ACRES field, not a measurement of the unioned shape.

features.name: Hetch Hetchy Water and Power
features.derived: the union of 32 published CPAD holdings. The parcels are CPAD's; the union is ours, and the acreage quoted is the sum of the holdings' own ACRES field, not a measurement of the unioned shape.

features.name: Hetch Hetchy Aqueduct
caveats: This named feature ENDS AT MOCCASIN (longitude -120.2653), not at Hetch Hetchy Reservoir (-119.789). It is 190.00 km — about 118 miles — of the system the city calls its 150-mile aqueduct. The upper Mountain Tunnel reach is not part of the named feature, so a label reading '150 miles' beside this line would be describing a different object.

features.name: San Francisco International Airport
caveats: No legal or cadastral boundary for SFO is published anywhere, by anyone. The FAA's aviation services carry runways and aprons and never property. This polygon is an aviation FACILITY FOOTPRINT and is labelled as one.

Measured on this run, in the map's own frame: Caltrans 218 is 2,276 acres. The city's OWN register of the land it owns there — City Lands land_id 635, also in this file — is 4,540 acres, 2.0 times as large, and 91 % of the Caltrans footprint falls inside it. The Airport cites about 5,207 acres including submerged Bay land. So the two shapes do not disagree about the airport; they are answering two different questions, and the file ships both.
Caltrans ships a second SFO polygon, OBJECTID 208, 2,784 acres, which runs far east into the Bay. It is not the airport and it is not in this file.

corpus_check._: how many of the corpus's beats name each published shape. A shape with zero is geometry without a record behind it — still the city's land, but not the same kind of claim as Hetch Hetchy, and a component should not present the two alike.
corpus_check.counted: beat `quote` and `headline` — the Journal's own words. Our `note` text is swept separately and reported as in_our_notes_only, never as a hit.
corpus_check.traps: 'Colman' is a Supervisor and is not Colma; 'O'Shaughnessy' is the City Engineer far more often than the dam, so that pattern requires the word Dam.
